user.title: Remote syslog server
user.description: Home Assistant's own log rotates only at restart and keeps one previous copy, so a restart destroys the history. Send it to a syslog collector instead, where it is rotated and kept.

data_description.host: Hostname or IP address of the syslog collector.
data_description.protocol: UDP is what most collectors listen on by default. TCP confirms delivery and never drops a record, but requires the collector to accept it.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach that address. For TCP, check the collector is listening on that port; for UDP, check the hostname resolves.

init.title: Forwarding options
init.description: Everything at the chosen level and above is forwarded. Keep this at Warning for normal use and raise it while investigating something - a single integration at Debug can produce megabytes per hour.

data_description.level: Records below this level are not sent.
data_description.tag: Identifies Home Assistant in the collector's logs. The integration's logger name is appended automatically.
data_description.facility: Syslog facility to send under, so records can be routed or filtered by the collector. local0 keeps Home Assistant distinct from add-ons and network gear.
data_description.exclude_loggers: One logger name per line, matched by prefix - 'custom_components.foo' covers all of its child loggers. Use this to silence a known firehose. Exclusions take priority over the list below.
data_description.include_loggers: One per line, also matched by prefix. Leave empty to forward everything. Set this only when you want a narrow capture of specific integrations.
